scenario.briefing: The lab wants a small inventory command that can be built and run with Swift Package Manager without data races.

title: Package an async command-line tool
summary: Turn a library manifest into an executable package, protect shared counts with an actor, and repair a missing package dependency.

objectives.description: Apply Swift Package Manager source conventions.

hints: A product is what users build; a target is what the compiler builds.
An executable target must also appear in products.
An actor serializes access to its stored state.

misconceptions.description: Declaring a target but no executable product.
misconceptions.testDescription: The manifest declares an executable product and target.
misconceptions.feedback: Swift Package Manager needs both an executable target and an executable product that exposes it. A bare .target builds a library, not a command.

misconceptions.description: Using a class for state shared by concurrent tasks.
misconceptions.testDescription: The shared counter is an actor.
misconceptions.feedback: An actor protects its mutable state with actor isolation. A plain class requires manual synchronization and is not Sendable when it has mutable state.

misconceptions.description: Listing every source file in the manifest.
misconceptions.feedback: Swift Package Manager includes every Swift file under the target directory. Only exclude or customize paths when the default layout does not fit.

misconceptions.description: Using a product without declaring its package.
misconceptions.feedback: A target dependency on .product requires a matching .package entry in the manifest's dependencies. Renaming the product does not resolve the package.

sections.title: Products and targets
sections.body: Package.swift is a Swift manifest. A target is a compilation unit, and a product is what another package or the command line can build. An executable needs .executableTarget(name: "Inventory") in targets and .executable(name: "inventory", targets: ["Inventory"]) in products. The tools version line, such as // swift-tools-version: 6.0, selects the manifest API.

sections.title: Conventions find the files
sections.body: By default, the Inventory target reads Sources/Inventory. Every .swift file under that directory belongs to the target; adding a file needs no manifest edit. Resources use the resources parameter, and tests live under Tests/InventoryTests. swift build compiles, swift test runs tests, and swift run inventory launches the executable.

sections.title: Actors serialize shared state
sections.body: An actor is a reference type whose stored state is isolated. Calling actor methods from outside requires await, and the runtime serializes access. Mark mutable state private so callers cannot bypass isolation. Use a struct for values that should copy and an actor only when shared mutable state is genuinely needed.

steps.title: Build the executable package
steps.prompt: Edit Package.swift and Sources/Inventory/main.swift. Expose an inventory executable and protect the shared usage count with an actor.
hints: Keep the tools version and package name.
Add an executable product named inventory.
Make UsageCounter an actor and await its methods.

localVerification.description: Resolves and compiles the package, which fails if the product or target configuration is inconsistent.

tests.description: The manifest declares an executable product and target.
The shared counter is an actor.

steps.title: The unresolved product
steps.prompt: swift build fails because the target uses a product without declaring its package. Select the faulty instruction and the correct repair.
hints: A .product dependency names both a product and a package.
The package must be declared in the manifest dependencies first.
Renaming the product in the target does not add the package.

fixes.label: Rename the product to Inventory in the target dependency.
Change the product dependency to a branch reference.

steps.explanation: A product dependency resolves only after its package appears in the manifest's top-level dependencies. Renaming the product creates a different missing product.

steps.title: Add a source file
steps.prompt: A new file, Report.swift, is added under Sources/Inventory. What manifest change is required?
hints: Swift Package Manager uses directory conventions.
Every Swift file under the target directory is included.
Only exclusions and custom paths need to be listed.

quiz.prompt: A new file, Report.swift, is added under Sources/Inventory. What manifest change is required?

options.label: No change; the target includes every Swift file in its directory.
Add each source file to a sources array.
Move the file to the repository root.
Create a second target for the new file.

quiz.explanation: SwiftPM discovers Swift files by target directory. A custom path or exclusion list is needed only when the default layout is not used.
